prompt: Employees want a chatbot that answers questions from the company's 30,000 internal wiki pages, which are edited every day.
why: Index the pages as embeddings, retrieve the most relevant chunks per question, and answer from them.
trap: Fine-tuning on the wiki would be stale by tomorrow and still couldn't cite which page an answer came from.

prompt: A support assistant must answer from the current refund policy and show which section each answer came from.
tells: show which section each answer came from
why: Retrieval gives the model the exact passages, so it can quote and cite them.
trap: Guardrails can block bad answers, but they don't supply the right facts.

prompt: A legal team wants to ask questions across 4,000 contracts, far more text than fits in any model's context window.
tells: more text than fits in any model's context window
why: Retrieve only the few relevant contract sections for each question.
trap: Batch jobs can summarize every contract, but a live question needs the relevant passages, not all of them.

prompt: A product assistant keeps inventing specs for products launched after the model's training cutoff.
tells: launched after the model's training cutoff
why: The model simply doesn't know new products; retrieve the catalog entry and ground the answer in it.
trap: Evals will measure the hallucinations; they won't fix the missing knowledge.

prompt: A sales assistant keeps quoting last quarter's pricing. Prices change every few weeks, and the latest price sheet lives in a shared drive.
why: Retrieve the current price sheet at question time; the model's own knowledge can't keep up.
trap: Fine-tuning bakes in a snapshot that's stale in weeks.

prompt: Each customer should be able to ask questions about only their own uploaded contracts, never anyone else's.
why: Retrieve from a per-customer index (filtered by tenant) and answer from those passages.
trap: You can't fine-tune a model per customer; retrieval with access filters keeps data separate.

prompt: A support bot misses answers when users type exact error codes like "E-4071", though it handles paraphrased questions well.
why: Embeddings blur exact tokens; add keyword (BM25) search alongside vector search in the retriever.
trap: The fix is in retrieval, not in the prompt.

prompt: Answers about a long policy often cite a heading but miss the rule, which was cut into the next chunk during indexing.
tells: cite a heading but miss the rule
cut into the next chunk during indexing
why: Chunk on section boundaries or with overlap so related text stays together.
trap: The model is answering faithfully from bad chunks.

prompt: A team wants the model to know their 500-page employee handbook, which is updated monthly. Someone proposes fine-tuning on it.
why: Changing facts belong in retrieval; fine-tuning teaches behavior and goes stale.
trap: The trap: fine-tuning is mentioned, but the right answer is RAG.
